expected_level_description: You can: - compare and select the most appropriate delivery methods and processes - recognise, reflect and adapt when something does not work, encouraging experimentation - use a blended approach depending on the context - help teams to measure, evaluate and visualise outcomes - encourage reflective practice to improve ways of working

You can: - act as the point of contact for contracted suppliers - understand appropriate internal contacts and processes within a government department - understand how and when third parties should be brought into digital, data and technology projects

skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations - manage active and reactive communication - support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders
You can: - balance cost versus value - consider the impact of user needs - report on financial delivery - monitor cost and budget - understand how and when to escalate issues

You can: - manage the delivery of products and services that add value through different phases of the life cycle, with some support - identify if the product or service should move to the next phase and, if it should, how to do this - ensure the product or service is developed in line with the appropriate service standards for a phase - use new information to adapt approaches to life cycle management

You can: - facilitate the delivery flow of a team, managing the pace and tempo - actively address internal and external risks, issues and dependencies including where ownership exists outside the team

You can: - identify and challenge organisational processes of increasing complexity and those processes that are unnecessarily complicated - add value and can coach the organisation to inspect and adapt processes - guide teams through the implementation of a new process

You can: - understand the environment and prioritise the most important or high value tasks - use data to inform planning - manage complex internal and external dependencies - provide delivery confidence - remove blockers or impediments that affect plans and can develop a plan for difficult situations - ensure that teams plan appropriately for their capacity

You can: - effectively bring people together to form a motivated team - help to create the right environment for a team to work in and can empower them to deliver - recognise and deal with issues - help create the best team makeup depending on the situation

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - record and update risks for your area - suggest controls and track actions
